A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TimeMCL research work, including complete Appendices A–C. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-process experiments, six real-world forecasting benchmarks and cryptocurrency evaluations, including Figure 2 and Tables 1 and 12.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised benchmark scores and cryptocurrency forecast examples.

M1.justification: The multi-head architecture, WTA objective and its relaxed and annealed variants, scoring heads and inference procedure remain unchanged. Added implementation disclosures do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic processes, six benchmark datasets and 15-asset cryptocurrency corpus. Changed cryptocurrency illustrations select assets already present in that corpus.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: ETS where applicable, DeepAR, TimeGrad, TempFlow, Trf.TempFlow and Tactis2. The synthetic quantization references are also retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2.2 removes the 1/N factor from the absolute-target denominator used in CRPS-Sum, changing its stated normalization. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed; evaluation splits, budgets and hypothesis-count settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The cryptocurrency case study in Figures 4 and 6 is revised with different forecast trajectories and EOS replacing XMR among illustrated assets. Tables 4 and 9 also refresh the existing hypothesis-count sensitivity results, without adding a new analysis question.

E5.justification: Table 4 changes its reported training-seed count from three to four. Table 9 already stated four in v1, so this resolves a reporting inconsistency without establishing that additional runs occurred. Other uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 3, 4, 6–9 and 11 substantially revise numerical results and some rankings. ELECTRICITY's K=16 distortion winner changes from Tactis2 to TimeGrad; Table 7 revises TimeMCL(R.) SOLAR RMSE from 3100.51 to 3639.23, with TimeGrad now best. Cryptocurrency forecast examples are replaced, while aggregate cryptocurrency and computational-cost results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2.2 revises the mathematical definition of the CRPS denominator from mean absolute target magnitude to its total sum. The functional-quantization propositions, assumptions and proofs in Section 5 and Appendix A remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: adapting WTA to forecasting, interpreting TimeMCL as a functional quantizer, and producing diverse forecasts efficiently.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 replaces the interpretation that Figure 6 captures rare modes, specifically its last row, with the narrower statement that it captures different modes. Existing limitations concerning scaling and a predefined number of hypotheses remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3.1 newly specifies gradient-norm clipping at 10 for all models. Appendix C.4 discloses using the final cryptocurrency training checkpoint because validation losses decreased monotonically. These are additional reproducibility details, without evidence that the procedures changed.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning relative to prior forecasting and multiple-choice-learning research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized edits to the results discussion, appendix explanations, captions and acknowledgements, including an additional funding acknowledgement. The section structure and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 receive revised forecast plots, illustrated assets and axis ranges. Running title headers are added, with minor text reflow; the overall figure and table organization is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting consistency by correcting the CRPS normalization and reconciling the seed counts in Tables 4 and 9. Added clipping and checkpoint details improve reproducibility, and Section 6.2 better matches the revised results. These are limited gains; the broad score replacements are insufficiently explained to establish stronger empirical validation.
